profile.summary: DNABERT-S is a DNA embedding model that turns a DNA sequence into a single vector so that sequences from the same species end up close together. It starts from the DNABERT-2 genome foundation model and is further trained with contrastive learning on pairs of sequences from the same microbial species. The embeddings are meant for tasks such as species clustering, few-shot species classification and metagenomics binning, where many species have no reference genome.

summary_quotes.text: DNABERT-S builds upon a pre-trained genome foundation model named DNABERT-2.
since many real-world species remain uncharacterized, lacking known genomes for reference
Each training sample of DNABERT-S is a pair of non-overlapping DNA sequences extracted from the same species.
including species classification/identification, metagenomics binning, and understanding evolutionary relationships

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: DNABERT-S starts from the pretrained DNABERT-2 model and continues training it with contrastive learning on pairs of DNA sequences taken from the same species. Training follows a two-phase curriculum (curriculum contrastive learning): first a Weighted SimCLR objective pulls same-species sequences together and pushes different species apart, then a Manifold Instance Mixup (MI-Mix) objective mixes hidden representations at a randomly chosen layer to make harder examples. The resulting embedding, the mean of the last hidden states, can be clustered or fed to a simple classifier to separate species without reference genomes, for example in metagenomics binning.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is one released checkpoint, zhihan1996/DNABERT-S, which this page read at revision 00e47f96. The repository provides the training and evaluation data through gdown links and the scripts used for training, clustering, classification and binning. The README pins transformers 4.27 and suggests uninstalling triton on GPUs other than the A100. The arXiv record has three versions, and the HTML full text read here carries a different title from the README (DNABERT-S: Pioneering Species Differentiation with Species-Aware DNA Embeddings). A result should name the checkpoint revision.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: DNA embedding model: a genome foundation model further trained so that its sequence embeddings group DNA by species.

quotes.text: DNABERT-S is a foundation model based on [DNABERT-2](https://github.com/Zhihan1996/DNABERT_2) specifically designed for generating DNA embedding that naturally clusters and segregates genome of different species in the embedding space
DNABERT-S builds upon a pre-trained genome foundation model named DNABERT-2.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: BERT-style encoder whose config.json gives zhihan1996/DNABERT-2-117M as its starting checkpoint: 12 layers, hidden size 768, intermediate size 3072, 12 attention heads, vocabulary 4096; config.json sets alibi_starting_size and max_position_embeddings to 512 and position_embedding_type to absolute. The saved paper and README do not mention ALiBi. The model code is loaded from the Hugging Face repository.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A DNA sequence as a string, tokenised by the model's own tokenizer.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-token hidden states of size 768; the sequence embedding is their mean (mean pooling), a 768-value vector.

run_guide.summary: Set up the repository's environment at a pinned commit and compute a mean-pooled embedding for one DNA sequence with the published checkpoint.
prerequisites: conda, to create a Python 3.9 environment.

The packages in requirements.txt, including transformers==4.27 and torch. The README suggests uninstalling triton on GPUs other than the A100. The paper reports that the predictions in its species classification comparison took about 1 hour on 2 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; memory needs are not stated.
Weights are Apache-2.0 and not gated; no licence is stated for the code.

steps.title: Compute an embedding
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("zhihan1996/DNABERT-S", trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("zhihan1996/DNABERT-S", trust_remote_code=True)

dna = "ACGTAGCATCGGATCTATCTATCGACACTTGGTTATCGATCTACGAGCATCTCGTTAGC"
inputs = tokenizer(dna, return_tensors = 'pt')["input_ids"]
hidden_states = model(inputs)[0] # [1, sequence_length, 768]

# embedding with mean pooling
embedding_mean = torch.mean(hidden_states[0], dim=0)
print(embedding_mean.shape) # expect to be 768
PY
steps.explanation: The README's two Quick Start snippets joined in one shell heredoc: load the model and tokenizer from Hugging Face, then embed one sequence.

outputs: The shape of the mean-pooled embedding, which the README expects to be 768.
